Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 48, verses 1–3:

The opening of this surah begins with a mention of a grace and bounty upon the Prophet ﷺ. He was granted a manifest victory (al-fath al-mubin), and all his past and future sins were forgiven. His blessings upon him were completed, he was given a lasting guidance, and he was granted a mighty help and victory. This is the reward for the deep tranquility and patience with which he acted upon the divine instructions, and for the fact that he fully acted upon the revelation and the inspirations and guidance from Allah, abandoned all his own desires and intentions, and placed complete trust in Allah's watchful care. He saw a dream, and in accordance with it he set out. His she-camel sat down, and the people cried out that al-Qaswa' had refused to move, had become obstinate. But the Prophet ﷺ took from this a different sign. "Al-Qaswa' has not become obstinate, nor is that her habit, but she has been stopped by the One who stopped the elephant from Makkah. If the Quraysh today offer me any arrangement in which ties of kinship are requested, I will accept it." Umar ibn al-Khattab, in great agitation, asks him: "Are we not being humiliated in our religion?" The Prophet ﷺ replies: "I am the servant of Allah, and His Messenger. I cannot oppose His command, and, Insha Allah, He will not abandon me." This was the matter of the treaty. But when the news came that Uthman ؓ had been killed, the Prophet ﷺ said: "We will remain steadfast until we take revenge on the people." People were called to give the pledge (bay'ah). This pledge became known as the Bay'at al-Ridwan, and through it good came to those who took part, and it was an elevated rank for those who participated in it.

This surah was in reality a great victory, and the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah was in reality a great victory, because as a result the door to countless conquests was opened. It was also a victory from the perspective of the call to Islam. Imam al-Zuhri says that the victories Islam had previously achieved were smaller than this one. Before this, whenever people met, there was war. When peace was concluded, the state of war ended, people gained security from one another, and mixing and interaction became free, they began debate and dialogue on the subject of Islam. Whoever spoke reasonably about Islam entered it. Between the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah and the conquest, within two years, so many people became Muslims that their number equalled or exceeded all the Muslims of the previous period.

Ibn Hisham says that the proof of al-Zuhri's statement is that, according to Jabir ibn Abdullah, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ set out on the Hudaybiyyah expedition with fourteen hundred people, but exactly two years later, when Makkah was attacked, there were more than ten thousand men with him. In this period Khalid ibn al-Walid and Amr ibn al-As ؓ embraced Islam.

On earth, this victory meant that the Muslims were protected from the evil of the Quraysh, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had the opportunity to purify the Arabian Peninsula of the remaining dangers posed by the Jews. Banu Qaynuqa', Banu al-Nadir and Banu Qurayzah had been eliminated earlier. This danger now lay in the secure fortresses of Khaybar, because those fortresses of Khaybar were located on the route to Syria. Therefore, after Hudaybiyyah, Allah gave the territory of Khaybar to the Muslims as well. The Prophet ﷺ distributed the lands and spoils of Khaybar only among those who had taken part in Hudaybiyyah, and gave nothing to anyone else.

This was a victory of the Muslims of Madinah over the Quraysh of Makkah in a long war. Ustadh Muhammad Darwazah, in his book Sirat al-Rasul, says:

"There is no doubt that this peace, which the Noble Qur'an called a victory, must be considered a victory in every sense. The truth is that it should be counted among the decisive events of the Prophet's biography. This event became, in the history of Islam, the cause of Islam's strength and stability. In any case, it was a very beneficial event. Through this treaty, the Quraysh for the first time recognised the Islamic state and the status of the Prophet ﷺ, and they accepted the Muslims as a power equal to themselves; indeed, the Quraysh defended the Islamic state. In the two years before this, the Quraysh had twice attacked Madinah, and the Battle of the Confederates (al-Ahzab) had occurred one year before Hudaybiyyah, in which the Quraysh came against Madinah with countless confederate tribes in order to uproot the believers and Islam. During the Battle of the Confederates, there was extreme agitation in the ranks of the believers, and a general unease arose, because the number of those attacking Madinah was very great, and the Battle of the Confederates had an effect on the whole Arab world, because all the Arabs followed the Quraysh, and they were influenced by the harsh stance of the Quraysh. If one considers that the villagers around Madinah and the hypocrites were making prophecies that the Muslims would in no way return safe and sound from that battle, and they harboured every kind of ill thought, then in that context the importance of this victory becomes even clearer, and its far-reaching effects become evident."

"The subsequent events proved that the inspiration of the Prophet ﷺ was correct, and the Qur'an also confirmed it. Because of this peace, the Muslims obtained very great material, spiritual and missionary benefits. Moreover, from the military and political standpoint, the position of the Muslims became very strong. In the eyes of the tribes, the Muslims became a firm power, and as soon as they returned, the tribes around Madinah who had stayed behind came and began to present excuses. The voice of the hypocrites inside Madinah began to be suppressed, and they became weak. From every side, Arab delegations began to come into the presence of the Prophet ﷺ, and the power of the Jews was removed from Khaybar and its surrounding areas. These people had been spread along the route to Syria. It became possible for the Messenger ﷺ to send military expeditions to far-off regions such as Najd, Yemen and al-Balqa'. And exactly two years later the Messenger ﷺ conquered Makkah with an army of ten thousand. This was a decisive victory, when the help of Allah came, the conquest was completed, and people began to enter the religion of Allah in throngs."

I say that apart from all these aspects, there is another aspect from which this was a great victory. Through it, the hearts and minds of people were conquered for Islam. As a result, the event of the Bay'at al-Ridwan took place, in which the Muslims pledged upon death and not fleeing, and Allah announced that He was pleased with those who pledged under the tree. This announcement was recorded in the Qur'an, and then the features and qualities of the revolutionary leadership of Muhammad ﷺ and his revolutionary community were recorded in this surah as a result of this victory.

﴿Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and those who are with him are severe against the disbelievers and merciful among themselves. You see them bowing and prostrating, seeking the bounty of Allah and His pleasure. The marks of prostration are upon their faces, by which they are distinguished. This is their description in the Torah, and their example in the Gospel is that they are like a seed which sends forth its shoot, then strengthens it, then it grows thick, then stands firm upon its stalk, pleasing the sowers, so that through them He may enrage the disbelievers. Allah has promised, to those of them who believe and do righteous deeds, forgiveness and a great reward﴾ (48:29).

I say that in the history of the Islamic call this is a very great victory that any community has attained. Its effects continued to emerge in Islamic history for a long time.

Then, as a result, Surah al-Fath was revealed, with which the Prophet ﷺ was very pleased. The rains of Allah's mercy fell upon the Prophet ﷺ, so that his past and future faults were forgiven, and the believing companions received the favour that Allah was pleased with them. The Prophet ﷺ was given complete guidance and a great help, and then the community of believers was given the certificate of the Torah, the Gospel and the Qur'an. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Last night a surah was revealed to me which is more precious than all the wealth upon which the sun has ever risen." He thanked his Lord, and on account of these blessings he would pray very lengthy prayers. Aisha ؓ says that when the Messenger of Allah would stand to pray, his feet would swell. Aisha ؓ said to him that Allah had forgiven his past and future sins, so why did he exert himself so much? The Prophet ﷺ replied: "O Aisha! Should I not be a grateful servant?"

This was the opening, which concerned the Prophet ﷺ. After this, it is described how, through this victory, Allah bestowed great favours upon the Muslims, and how by His power He sent down tranquility upon their hearts. And in the Hereafter, for them there will be this forgiveness and the great success.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 48, verses 4–5:

The word "sakinah" (tranquillity) points to a meaningful expression, an image and a reflection. When tranquillity descends upon a heart, that heart becomes content, joyful and dignified. It attains certainty, trust and steadfastness. As a result, it bows in submission and is pleased with every command of Allah. Such a person then becomes exceedingly dignified.

The hearts of the Muslims were stirred by this event for several reasons, and they were under the pressure of various kinds of impressions. First, people had interpreted the Prophet's (ﷺ) dream to mean that he would enter Masjid al-Haram in that very year. Then the Quraysh set a condition that the Prophet (ﷺ) should return this year and perform 'Umrah the following year, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) accepted this condition, even though they had put on the ihram and garlanded the sacrificial animals (hady) with markers. These matters were unbearable for some emotional people. It is narrated that 'Umar (رضي الله عنه) came to Abu Bakr (رضي الله عنه), who was then in a state of great agitation, and said: "Did we not hear that we would go to the House of Allah and perform tawaf?" Abu Bakr (رضي الله عنه), whose heart beat in unison with that of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), said: "Did the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say that you would perform 'Umrah this very year?" 'Umar said: "He did not say it for this year." Abu Bakr (رضي الله عنه) said: "Then you will come and perform tawaf." So 'Umar left Abu Bakr and went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "Did you not tell us that we would go to the House of Allah and perform tawaf?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed. But did I say that you would perform 'Umrah this very year?" 'Umar said: "No." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Surely you will come and perform tawaf." These were the matters that were boiling in their hearts like lava.

Then the believers were also deeply angered by the conditions of the Quraysh: that if a Muslim came to Muhammad (ﷺ) with the permission of his guardian, he would be returned, but if a Muslim went to Makkah without the permission of the Muslims, he would not be returned. Then, because of their jahiliyyah, they had the phrase "Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim" struck out and replaced with "Bismika Allahumma." Then they had the words "Rasul Allah" removed from after your name. It is narrated that 'Ali (رضي الله عنه) refused to erase the words "(Rasul Allah)" as Suhayl had asked. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) himself erased them and said: "O Allah, You know that I am a Messenger."

The bravery of the Muslims, their zeal for the religion, their spirit of jihad and their readiness to fight the polytheists were evident from the collective pledge (bay'ah) they made. But since the matter ended suddenly in a truce, peace and return, the Muslims could not bear it calmly. Therefore their feelings were expressed. Thus, despite the command of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), they did not make sacrifices or shave their heads, even though the Prophet (ﷺ) issued the command three times. Yet they were people who would lay down their lives for the commands of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). The report that 'Urwah ibn Mas'ud al-Thaqafi gave to the Quraysh showed the condition of the Muslims. And the state was such that only when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) slaughtered his sacrifice and shaved his head did they then slaughter their animals and shave their heads. In short, this event had shaken them severely. Now that they had returned to obedience, they were still dismayed.

These people had set out from Madinah with the intention of 'Umrah. They had no intention of fighting; neither psychologically nor materially were they prepared for war. But when the Quraysh adopted a harsh stance, then news came that 'Uthman (رضي الله عنه) had been killed. Then the Quraysh sent some men who threw arrows and stones at the army of the Muslims. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called for the pledge to fight, they readily prepared with all their hearts. But this pledge does not prove that the state of war did not come suddenly upon the Muslims. This state of war was entirely sudden; these people had not gone out for battle. For this reason too, enthusiasm and fervour arose in the hearts of the Muslims. They were fourteen hundred, while the Quraysh were in their homes, and the polytheists of the surrounding areas of Makkah were their helpers and supporters.

When a person keeps all these circumstances in view and reflects upon this verse:

"It is He who sent down tranquillity into the hearts of the believers" (48:4), he perceives the beauty and sweetness of both the wording and the meaning, and the situation of that time also settles fully in his mind, and he clearly feels how the coolness of that tranquillity must have instantly soothed the burning hearts and restored them.

Since Allah knew the condition of the hearts of the Muslims and why it was so, that the agitation was the agitation of faith, and the love and zeal were Islamic zeal and the honour of faith, not for any worldly interest or for jahiliyyah, therefore Allah sent down this tranquillity.

"That they may increase in faith along with their faith" (48:4). Tranquillity is the rank that comes after the zeal of faith. It contains complete confidence. There is no restlessness; it is a contentment founded upon trust and certainty.

This is why it is made clear that victory and dominance are neither impossible nor difficult. If the wisdom of Allah required it, it would be very easy for Allah. Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 48, verses 4–5:

The word "sakinah" (tranquillity) points to a meaningful expression, an image and a reflection. When tranquillity descends upon a heart, that heart becomes content, joyful and dignified. It attains certainty, trust and steadfastness. As a result, it bows in submission and is pleased with every command of Allah. Such a person then becomes exceedingly dignified.

The hearts of the Muslims were stirred by this event for several reasons, and they were under the pressure of various kinds of impressions. First, people had interpreted the Prophet's (ﷺ) dream to mean that he would enter Masjid al-Haram in that very year. Then the Quraysh set a condition that the Prophet (ﷺ) should return this year and perform 'Umrah the following year, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) accepted this condition, even though they had put on the ihram and garlanded the sacrificial animals (hady) with markers. These matters were unbearable for some emotional people. It is narrated that 'Umar (رضي الله عنه) came to Abu Bakr (رضي الله عنه), who was then in a state of great agitation, and said: "Did we not hear that we would go to the House of Allah and perform tawaf?" Abu Bakr (رضي الله عنه), whose heart beat in unison with that of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), said: "Did the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say that you would perform 'Umrah this very year?" 'Umar said: "He did not say it for this year." Abu Bakr (رضي الله عنه) said: "Then you will come and perform tawaf." So 'Umar left Abu Bakr and went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "Did you not tell us that we would go to the House of Allah and perform tawaf?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed. But did I say that you would perform 'Umrah this very year?" 'Umar said: "No." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Surely you will come and perform tawaf." These were the matters that were boiling in their hearts like lava.

Then the believers were also deeply angered by the conditions of the Quraysh: that if a Muslim came to Muhammad (ﷺ) with the permission of his guardian, he would be returned, but if a Muslim went to Makkah without the permission of the Muslims, he would not be returned. Then, because of their jahiliyyah, they had the phrase "Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim" struck out and replaced with "Bismika Allahumma." Then they had the words "Rasul Allah" removed from after your name. It is narrated that 'Ali (رضي الله عنه) refused to erase the words "(Rasul Allah)" as Suhayl had asked. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) himself erased them and said: "O Allah, You know that I am a Messenger."

The bravery of the Muslims, their zeal for the religion, their spirit of jihad and their readiness to fight the polytheists were evident from the collective pledge (bay'ah) they made. But since the matter ended suddenly in a truce, peace and return, the Muslims could not bear it calmly. Therefore their feelings were expressed. Thus, despite the command of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), they did not make sacrifices or shave their heads, even though the Prophet (ﷺ) issued the command three times. Yet they were people who would lay down their lives for the commands of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). The report that 'Urwah ibn Mas'ud al-Thaqafi gave to the Quraysh showed the condition of the Muslims. And the state was such that only when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) slaughtered his sacrifice and shaved his head did they then slaughter their animals and shave their heads. In short, this event had shaken them severely. Now that they had returned to obedience, they were still dismayed.

These people had set out from Madinah with the intention of 'Umrah. They had no intention of fighting; neither psychologically nor materially were they prepared for war. But when the Quraysh adopted a harsh stance, then news came that 'Uthman (رضي الله عنه) had been killed. Then the Quraysh sent some men who threw arrows and stones at the army of the Muslims. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called for the pledge to fight, they readily prepared with all their hearts. Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 48, verses 6–7:

After this, another aspect of Allah's wisdom in that event comes into view: that He would punish the hypocrite men and women, and that the polytheist men and women would be exposed to such acts that they become deserving of punishment.

﴿And He punishes the hypocrite men and hypocrite women, and the polytheist men and polytheist women, who harbour an evil opinion about Allah. Upon them is a turn of evil; Allah is angry with them, has cursed them, and has prepared for them Hell, and evil is it as a destination. To Allah belong the hosts of the heavens and the earth, and Allah is Mighty and Wise.﴾

In this verse, Allah has joined the polytheist men and women and the hypocrite men and women in the attribute of evil opinion, and in the attribute that they did not believe that Allah would help the believers. Therefore Allah has also included them in this punishment: the turn of evil has come upon them, and they have been encircled by it themselves. This evil is going to fall upon them, and Allah's anger is upon all of them, Allah's curse is upon all of them, their final end is also evil, and they share in it. This is because hypocrisy is a most base act. It is equal to shirk, rather it is worse than shirk, and it is a degraded act. In harming the Muslims, the role of these hypocrite men and women is not less than that of the polytheist men and women, although the scope and nature of their harms differ.

Allah has declared the important attribute of the hypocrite men and women and the polytheist men and women to be that they harbour evil opinions about Allah. The believer holds good opinion of his Lord and always seeks good from Allah, and expects good whether his circumstances are good or he is in difficulty. He strengthens his faith so that in both conditions he seeks goodness from Allah, because his heart is attached to Allah, and Allah never closes the spring of goodness. When a person's heart is connected to Allah, he perceives this reality and directly tastes its flavour. As for the hypocrite and the polytheist, they do not possess the blessing of connection with Allah. Therefore they do not perceive this reality, nor do they find it within themselves. So they harbour evil opinions about Allah, and they judge only by outward matters and base their decisions on apparent circumstances. When some outward signs appear to them, they expect that misfortune has befallen them and also the Muslims. They have no trust in Allah's decree and planning, although Allah's decree and planning sometimes work out of sight.

In this verse, Allah has gathered together the various kinds of the enemies of Islam and the Muslims, described their state, explained how dreadful their end is, and at the end stated that their evil opinion is mistaken. Allah's power is vast and His wisdom far-reaching.

﴿And to Allah belong the hosts of the heavens and the earth, and Allah is Mighty and Wise.﴾ Therefore no scheme of these enemies of Islam can overpower Allah, and no activity of theirs is hidden from Him. He is the Master of the powers of the heavens and the earth, and He is Mighty and Wise.

After this, the address turns to the Prophet ﷺ regarding what his duty is, and what the duties of the believers are in this regard. You (ﷺ) have conveyed Allah's message to them. They have believed, and they have also pledged allegiance directly to Allah in the Bay'ah al-Ridwan. They made this covenant directly with Allah, so this is a most exalted station they have attained. Let them remember that the responsibilities of this pledge and covenant are also great.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 48, verses 8–9:

O Prophet (ﷺ), those who were pledging allegiance to you were in fact pledging allegiance to Allah. The hand of Allah was upon their hands. Now, whoever breaks this covenant, the consequence of his breaking of the covenant will fall upon his own self, and whoever fulfils the covenant he has made with Allah, Allah will soon grant him a great reward.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is a witness over all the people to whom he has been sent. He will bear witness that the message with which he was sent, he conveyed to the people, and that the response of the people has been this: some of them became believers, some adopted disbelief, and some adopted hypocrisy; some accepted reform, and some remained corrupters as before. So just as the Prophet (ﷺ) fulfilled the right of prophethood and conveyed the message, in the same way he (ﷺ) will bear witness, because he (ﷺ) is a bringer of good tidings (mubashshir) and a giver of glad news, of a good end and of Allah's forgiveness and a good end for those who believed and obeyed, and a warner (nadhir) to the disbelievers, the hypocrites and the corrupt rebels, that their end will be evil. Upon them will be the wrath of Allah, a curse, and a severe punishment.

This is the official duty of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). After this, the address turns to the believers: what are your duties in regard to the Messenger? That you believe in Allah and His Messenger (ﷺ); then fulfil the requirements of faith; help Allah and His Messenger (ﷺ) in the establishment of the Islamic system; show the utmost respect to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ); and glorify and extol Allah morning and evening, that is, serve Allah the whole day, because by mentioning both ends of the day, the whole day is intended. That is, remain attached to Allah at all times. This is the fruit and result of faith which is expected from every believer, and the Messenger has been sent as a witness, a bringer of good tidings and a warner for exactly this purpose.

The very purpose of the coming of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was to establish a connection between the people and Allah, and to arrange such a pledge and such a covenant that this connection would remain established even after he (ﷺ) departed. When people place their hand upon the hand of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and pledge allegiance, it is as though they placed their hand upon the hand of Allah and pledged allegiance.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 48, verse 10:

Inna alladhina yubayi'unaka ... fawqa aydihim (48:10): "Verily, those who pledge allegiance to you, [O Prophet], are in fact pledging allegiance to Allah; the hand of Allah is above their hands."

This fact makes the pledge (bay'ah) between the Muslims and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) very lofty and weighty, because the hand of Allah is upon the hands of the people: in this contract Allah Himself was a party. Allah was the One receiving the pledge, and the hand of Allah was above the hands of those who pledged. And, by Allah, how great is His Being, Allah, the Lord of Majesty and Honour! His hand!

With this awareness and this conception, the very thought of breaking this covenant leaves the human heart, even if the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) should pass from this world. Allah is, in any case, present. He is indeed the real party to this covenant, and He is its Overseer.

Faman nakatha fa-innama yankuthu 'ala nafsihi (48:10): "Whoever breaks his oath, breaks it only to his own detriment." The loss falls upon him alone. In the bargain that took place between him and Allah, the party that stands to lose is himself. Allah is free of need from both worlds. Therefore, if he breaks this covenant, the harm will be to him; he will deserve the wrath of Allah and His punishment, because Allah does not love those who break their word; Allah loves those who keep their covenants and are faithful.

Wa man awfa ... ajran 'azima (48:10): "And whoever fulfils what he has covenanted with Allah, Allah will soon grant him a great reward." It will be a great reward in an absolute sense, without any measure of detail, because the One making this covenant is great, so His reward is also great, great by the reckoning of Allah. A human being cannot conceive of the greatness of that reward and of the One who bestows it. A human being can neither conceive of the greatness of Allah nor of the great measures of Allah, because the human being is himself small and his conception is small.

When the discussion of the reality of the bay'ah reached the matter of loyalty and disloyalty, there began mention of those who showed disloyalty on that occasion, namely the people living in the villages around Madinah, who refused to set out with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on the journey to Hudaybiyah, because they had evil thoughts about Allah. They expected that the believers who were going on that occasion would fall into calamity and suffer loss, as they went to the Quraysh at their homes. Before this, the Quraysh had for two consecutive years come to Madinah and fought the Muslims. In this surah the Prophet (ﷺ) has been informed in advance what excuses these people will offer when you and your companions return to Madinah safe and sound. Their thought was that the Muslims would never return, although the Quraysh then concluded a ten-year truce with the Muslims. Although the conditions appeared to be against the Muslims, in reality the Quraysh retreated from their position; they accepted the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the Muslims as their equals, and by making peace they freed themselves from enmity.

In any case, here Allah tells the real reasons for these people's not going out and lays them bare before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the Muslims. It is also told that those who went out with you in this campaign have a good future: in the future they alone will receive abundant spoils of war, conquests and successes, and those who remained behind from this expedition will be deprived of them. In the future, in easy campaigns, these Bedouins will want to come out with you for battle so that they may obtain a share of the spoils. You are directed not to accept their offer in the easy campaigns, and in the coming campaigns to take with you only those who took part at Hudaybiyah. It is also told here that if you are truly people who wage jihad, you will be given the opportunity to fight a severely powerful enemy; if you truly wish to fight, then set out at that time. There Allah will give you your share. If they obey at that time, they will deserve a great reward.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 48, verses 11-16:

﴿O Prophet (ﷺ), those among the desert Arabs who were left behind will certainly say to you: "Our possessions and our families kept us busy, so ask forgiveness for us." They say with their tongues what is not in their hearts. Say: "Then who has any power to prevent Allah's decision regarding you, if He intends harm for you or intends benefit for you? Indeed, Allah is fully aware of what you do." Rather, you thought that the Messenger and the believers would never return to their families, and this idea appealed to your hearts, and you entertained evil thoughts, and you were a people ruined.﴾ Whoever does not believe in Allah and His Messenger (ﷺ), We have prepared a blazing Fire for such disbelievers. To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills, and He is Forgiving and Merciful.

﴿Those who were left behind will say, when you set out to take spoils: "Let us come with you." They want to change Allah's word. Say: "You will never follow us; Allah has already said this." They will say: "No, rather you envy us." But they hardly understand the truth.﴾ Say to the desert Arabs who were left behind: ﴿You will be called to fight a people of great might. You will fight them, or they will submit. If you obey, Allah will give you a good reward, but if you turn away again as you turned away before, He will punish you with a painful torment.﴾

The Qur'an has not merely recorded the statements of these people and refuted them. At this opportune moment it has also addressed their deep psychology, the doubts and thoughts that arose in their hearts, and then prescribed a remedy for them. The moral diseases within them have been diagnosed so that a suitable cure may be applied. The realities remain, and the fundamental principles of the Islamic worldview are made clear and preserved.

The villagers around Medina who remained behind, despite the invitation, at the occasion of Hudaybiyyah were the tribes of Ghifar, Muzaynah, Ashja' and Aslam, and others. The Qur'an says their excuse would be:

﴿Our possessions and our families kept us busy﴾ (48:11). This is not a valid excuse. Everyone always has property, children and family. If such excuses were accepted, then no one would find time for ideological work, for their belief, or for the responsibilities of the Islamic da'wah. Their second statement would be:

﴿So ask forgiveness for us﴾ (48:11). But even in this there is no truth, and it is said:

﴿They say with their tongues what is not in their hearts﴾ (48:11).

At this point they are told that Allah has a system of qada wa qadar (divine decree and predestination), and no one can prevent it. Remaining behind from battle cannot stop destiny, nor can any undertaking be stopped. You are surrounded within Allah's power. He acts as He wills, and He is aware of everything. He acts in accordance with His knowledge.

﴿Say: "Then who has any power to prevent Allah's decision regarding you, if He intends harm for you or intends benefit for you? Indeed, Allah is fully aware of what you do."﴾ (48:11)

In this question itself it is shown how a true believer should behave: he should submit before Allah's decisions, promptly carry out Allah's commands, and not hesitate or delay. Because delay and hesitation can neither avert any loss nor postpone any gain. And the fabrication of excuses is not hidden from Him. Allah gives reward and punishment according to His knowledge, so fabricated excuses have no effect before Him. This is most timely guidance, suited to the setting, and it is the Qur'an's method to rebuke at the most appropriate moment.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 48, verse 12:

بل ظننتم ان لن ۔۔۔۔۔۔ قوما بورا (48:12) "Nay, you thought that the Messenger and the believers would never return to their families, and this idea appealed to your hearts, and you entertained evil thoughts, and you became a people ruined (bur)."

Thus Allah strips these people bare. Their intentions and the state of their hearts are laid open before them. The calculations they had made are also told to them. The evil opinion they held about Allah in their hearts is also disclosed. Their belief was that the Messenger of Allah was pushing his companions into the jaws of death, and therefore would not return to Madinah. For these people were going into the mouths of those who had come to their homes and fought them, and who had killed the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in Madinah. Their reference was to Uhud and the Confederates (al-Ahzab).

These people had not reckoned with the power of Allah and the favours of Allah, and with how greatly Allah bestows His generosity upon His sincere servants. Moreover, they had considered matters in a secular way, and their hearts were empty of the Islamic outlook on life. In their view, duty and obligation were nothing at all. Yet the Islamic outlook has its demands, and every sacrifice should have seemed trivial to them. Furthermore, obedience to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and companionship with him should have been above the reckoning of profit and loss, gain and harm. This was a duty that they should have discharged regardless of the outcomes.

Nevertheless, they entertained suspicions, and evil opinion and suspicion were made attractive to them. They could see nothing beyond that suspicion. They did not think about any other event or any other aspect apart from that evil opinion, and this was their evil opinion. It arose because their hearts were corrupt. Here they are called "a people ruined (qawman bur)." This is a strange manner of expression. "Bur" refers to land that is barren, in which there is no growth: no trees or fruit, and no golden harvest. A heart in which there is no greenness of good opinion, which is not hopeful concerning Allah and holds no good opinion within it, is barren. It is dead, and in the end it is destined to be ruined and destroyed.

Even today some people think about the community of believers in this manner, the same kind of people who lived around Madinah, whose hearts were dry and had no spirit of life in them. When such people see that the scales of the falsehood-worshippers are heavier, and that most of the worldly powers are with the people of evil and of inner corruption, while the righteous are few in number, or poor in resources, or lacking in status, wealth and possessions, these bedouins and people of that sort think in this way in every age and place. Their thinking goes like this: since the followers of faith or the lovers of Islam confront great powers, and these powers appear very swollen, there is no hope for these handful of Muslims. Therefore, it is best to keep away from them. Such people always expect that today or tomorrow they will be uprooted and thrown away, and that this call will come to an end. So, as a precaution, they separate themselves from this path and take another road. But Allah always defeats the evil opinion of such people, and Allah changes the circumstances of His grace and by His plans prepares the way for His servants. Allah measures by His own measures, which are the true measures, and which are in His mighty hand. He lowers some people and raises others, and those who are disbelievers, hypocrites, and those who hold evil suspicions about Allah have no knowledge of this. Such people exist in every era and every age.

The true balance is the balance of faith. Allah tells these bedouin Muslims to weigh by this balance, and He determines the reward of deeds according to this balance; the mercy of Allah is with this balance. The moments of opportunity are few, so seek the mercy and forgiveness of Allah and benefit from them!

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 48, verses 13–14:

And whoever does not believe in Allah and His Messenger – then indeed, We have prepared for the disbelievers a blazing Fire. (48:13) And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills, and Allah is Forgiving and Merciful. (48:14)

"Those who do not believe in Allah and His Messenger (ﷺ), for such disbelievers We have prepared a blazing fire. The dominion of the heavens and the earth belongs to Allah alone; He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills, and He is Forgiving and Merciful."

These people used to put forward the excuse of their wealth and their families. So the question is: of what benefit will wealth and children be in that Hell which has been prepared for the disbelievers, if they did not believe in Allah and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)? In short, there are two pans of the scale: one is faith, and the other is disbelief, hypocrisy and evil assumption. Among these, they should accept one. The Allah who warns you is the Master of the powers of the heavens and the earth. He can punish, and He can also forgive.

Allah rewards or punishes people according to their deeds. But His will is absolute and free; there is no restriction upon it. This matter has been stated here so that it settles in the hearts of people that Allah is capable of everything, and that it is He who has determined the recompense for deeds. The mercy and forgiveness of Allah are near for all. It is fitting that people seek it, before the decree of Allah's punishment is issued, and this decree is clearly meant for those who do not believe in Allah and His Messenger (ﷺ).

After this, Allah points to the spoils of war which have been destined for the believers. This will be the very opposite of the circumstances of their evil assumptions, and from the style of the speech it appears that these events are to take place in a very near time.
