Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 48, verse 15:

سیقول المخلفون ۔۔۔۔۔۔ یفقھون الا قلیلا (48:15) "When you set out to take booty, those who were left behind will surely say, 'Let us come with you.' They wish to change the word of Allah. Say to them, 'You shall not follow us; Allah has already said this before.' They will say, 'No, you envy us.' (In fact the matter is not envy.) Rather, they understand little of the truth."

Most commentators hold that this refers to the conquest of Khaybar. It is possible that it is indeed Khaybar. Even if Khaybar is not what is meant, the meaning is that soon the Muslims will go on some expedition, and these people will say, "Let us go too."

The commentators mention Khaybar because the event of Khaybar took place immediately after the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah, for the conquest of Khaybar occurred in Muharram 7 AH, that is, two months after the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah. In it, a great deal of booty was obtained, and the fortresses of Khaybar were excluded from the Arabian Peninsula.

The commentators have related with consistent transmission (tawatur) that Allah had made a covenant with those who went on the expedition of Hudaybiyyah that no one else would share in the booty of Khaybar. However, there is no explicit text (nass) on this matter. Perhaps they derive this principle from practical events. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had reserved it for the People of Hudaybiyyah, and in that expedition he had not taken anyone else along.

Regardless, Allah told the Prophet (ﷺ) to reject the offer of the Bedouins who stayed behind when they wish to accompany him for the easily obtainable booty nearby. He decided that their going out is against the command of Allah, and gave advance notice that when the Prophet (ﷺ) rejects their offer, they will make the accusation: "You envy us." Bal tahsudunana, "Rather, you envy us." You do not take them on this expedition because you do not want to give us booty. At the same time, He immediately said that these people do not know the wisdom of Allah; they lack understanding. The wisdom of Allah is that those who stayed behind be afflicted with a measure of deprivation, and that obedient servants be given some rewards, so that they receive the reward of their obedience, because they obeyed in circumstances when death was seen plainly before them.

After this, Allah tells His Prophet to say to those who stayed behind that a further test remains for them. Soon an expedition will be sent against a mighty people, and you will be called to it. And these people will fight you for the sake of Islam. If you succeed in this test, there will be a reward for you as well. If you persist in disobedience even in this final test, then you will become deserving of a painful punishment forever.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 48, verse 16:

Say to the desert Arabs who were left behind: "You will soon be called to face a people of great might. You will fight them, or they will submit. If you obey, Allah will grant you a good reward, but if you turn away as you turned away before, He will punish you with a painful punishment." (48:16)

There is also a difference of opinion in its interpretation about who these people are, described as "of great might" (ulil-ba's ash-shadid), whether they belonged to the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) or to the time of the Rightly Guided Caliphs. The closer view is that they belonged to the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the purpose was to test the faith of the desert Arabs who lived around Madinah.

The important matter is not who they were. The important matter is: what is the Qur'an's method of training? How does the Qur'an treat sick hearts? How does the Qur'an give guidance, and how does it test people in practice? This is shown by the way the mental condition of those desert people is exposed before the firm Muslims, so that both they themselves and the Muslims come to know their state. Then they are guided to adopt a firm attitude in faith and action, and to embrace high values.

Since the matter was one of trial, Allah made departure (for jihad) obligatory upon all Muslims, and by specifying these people He made clear what a genuine excuse is. If anyone was left behind from jihad in accordance with that, there will be no punishment for him and no sin.

The blind man and the lame man are permanently excused and cannot go out for jihad, and the sick man is excused only temporarily; as long as he has not recovered he remains excused.

Asl (the essential matter) is that the lame man is permanently excused and cannot go out for jihad, and the sick man is temporarily excused.

The real matter is obedience and disobedience. The spirit of obedience and the intention of disobedience are matters connected with the heart and the psyche, not with outward forms or outward excuses. Whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger (ﷺ), his reward is Paradise, and whoever turns away should remember that a painful punishment awaits him. Everyone should weigh jihad and its hardships, the reward of jihad and sitting behind and its comforts, compare them with one another, and choose whichever of them he prefers.

Lesson No. 245 – At a Glance

This entire lesson is about the believers. It is a dialogue with the community that pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ beneath the tree, and in doing so pledged allegiance to Allah. Allah was present, was a witness to that pledge, confirmed and attested it, and the hand of Allah was upon the hands of those who pledged. This was the group of the Companions ؓ who heard with their own ears what Allah was saying to the Messenger of Allah about them:

﴿Indeed, Allah was pleased with the believers when they pledged allegiance to you under the tree. He knew what was in their hearts, so He sent down tranquility upon them and rewarded them with an imminent victory.﴾ (48:18) This is information to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about these believers and a dialogue with them, and it is good news that Allah has stored up for them very precious spoils. Many conquests are destined for them, and on this journey too He was their supporter and helper, and He will remain so in the future. According to His sunnah, Allah has kept continuous conquests in store for them, and the sunnah of Allah never changes. The passage also contains criticism of the disbelievers, and it states why Allah preferred a peace treaty on that occasion, and that the dream the Messenger ﷺ had seen was true: that the Muslims would enter the Sacred Mosque. They would enter in a most peaceful manner, and their religion would certainly prevail.

This lesson and this surah conclude with a description of the distinguished and unique community of Companions who carried out a revolutionary work alongside the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Their qualities are described with reference to the Torah and the Gospel, and at the end it is proclaimed that they have become deserving of forgiveness and a noble reward.

Today, fourteen hundred years later, I see on the horizon of Islamic history those sacred moments in which the whole universe is watching, as this news descends from the higher realm to the Prophet ﷺ and is conveyed to the Muslims. I try to read these pages of the universe and to see what was hidden within the conscience of the universe in those moments, because at that time the entire universe was in step with Allah's word that these chosen people, present at that particular piece of earth and pledging beneath the tree, are the salt of the earth.

With the eye of insight I wish to see the circumstances of those fortunate people of the earth who heard, with their own ears and personally, that Allah says about them, "I am pleased with them." Then the place where they were is also specified: beneath the tree, and that pledge is also specified.

﴿When they pledged allegiance to you under the tree﴾ (48:18). They heard these verses themselves from the tongue of their truthful Prophet, and glad tidings were given to them from Allah.

O Allah! How did those blessed beings spend those moments, and how did they listen to those words, in which the Divine Being Himself points to each person: "O so-and-so, O so-and-so, I am pleased with you; you are the one who pledged beneath the tree. I knew what was in your hearts. I then sent down tranquility upon you."

One of us reads this verse: "Allah is the Protector of those who believe" (Allah waliyy alladhina amanu), and he considers himself fortunate. He hopes in his heart that, God willing, he too is included in the general meaning of this verse, or someone reads or hears it.

"Indeed Allah is with the patient" (inna Allaha ma'a al-sabirin). Therefore he is reassured and says in his heart, "God willing, I too am among those who are patient." But those people were hearing it themselves, and the Prophet of God was reciting it to them; each one was hearing that Allah's intent was directed at him, and He was speaking to him, sending a message to him that He was pleased with him. Even though He knew what was in his soul, He was pleased with him.

O Allah, what a great honour this is!

﴿Allah was indeed pleased with the believers when they pledged allegiance to you under the tree. He knew what was in their hearts, so He sent down tranquility upon them and rewarded them with an imminent victory.﴾ (48:18) Allah knew that in their hearts there was fervour for His religion, not for their own selves. He knew that they were pledging with a sincere heart. Allah knew that the thoughts about war that arose within their hearts they were swallowing, and that with restraint they were carrying out the commands of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, standing behind him like obedient Muslims.

﴿Then He sent down tranquility upon them﴾ (48:18). This is a strange word and manner: tranquility was being sent down. Calm, composure, dignity and steadfastness were descending upon them. In such circumstances, with the heat of the sun, the stifling conditions, zeal and other emotions, people would have been restless, and this was replaced by coolness, contentment and joy.

﴿And rewarded them with an imminent victory﴾ (48:18). This treaty itself was a victory; from it many other conquests began. The conquest of Khaybar came immediately, and the prevailing view of the commentators is that this refers to the conquest of Khaybar.

The Quranic quotations are rendered plainly in English within the markers, Arabic technical terms are transliterated, and the passage is translated in full.

"And abundant spoils which they will take" (48:19). Either these spoils were obtained with the conquest, if the conquest meant is that of Khaybar, or they are the spoils of war acquired after the conquest. And if we consider this very treaty itself to be the conquest, since on account of this reconciliation the Muslims became free for many other conquests.

"And Allah is Mighty and Wise" (48:19). This is the outcome of all the verses; that is, in the promise of Allah's good pleasure, the conquest, and the countless spoils, the power, capability, wisdom and governance of Allah are at work. And it is through might and wisdom that Allah fulfils His promises.

After the announcement that Allah Himself has become pleased with those who pledged allegiance, the discourse now turns toward the believers themselves; now they are the ones addressed. Reconciliation, conquest, guidance and spoils are all mentioned, everything that is being given to them:

This is a clear glad tidings from Allah. The believers heard it, were fully convinced of it, and knew that a great deal had been prepared for them. After this they lived on and saw with their own eyes the fulfilment of these verses, because it was Allah's promise, and Allah's promise is never broken. Here Allah says that He has granted them this victory immediately. It may refer to the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah, as is related from Ibn 'Abbas, who said that Hudaybiyyah itself was the victory and the spoils. As we explained earlier, the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah was in reality a victory, and the circumstances in which it came about also made it a victory for the Muslims. It may also refer to the conquest of Khaybar, as is related from Mujahid, since after Hudaybiyyah this was the nearest booty that the Muslims received. The more preferred view is that the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah itself is called a victory.

Allah tells them that it is a very great favour of Allah upon them that He restrained the hands of people from touching them. Among them were the polytheists of Makkah and other people who were waiting for the right moment, hoping that the Muslims would become entangled in some trouble so that they could attack. At that time the Muslims were in small numbers, while the others were very numerous. Yet the Muslims fulfilled their pledge of allegiance and discharged their responsibilities. Therefore Allah restrained the hands of the people from them and kept them in safety.

﴿And that it might be a sign for the believers﴾ (48:20). This event, which at the beginning they had disliked very much and which lay upon their hearts like a heavy stone, Allah declares to be a miracle for them. In the days to come they will see its results, and those who obeyed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and submitted, even while disliking it, will receive its reward. They will know that it was a very great event, and the reward they receive will be very great, and tranquillity, peace and certainty will be poured into their hearts.

﴿And guide you to a straight path﴾ (48:20). This is because of your obedience, your submission and the sincerity of your intentions. Thus Allah announces a comprehensive reward for them: they will receive spoils of war and they will also be granted guidance. So goodness will come to them from every side. And this good and benefit will lie in the matter that they did not like and regarded as a heavy stone. Thus they are informed in advance that what Allah has chosen for them is in truth what is to be preferred. In this way they are trained to obey and carry out commands in every circumstance.

Besides these rewards and benefits, some other gains are also announced here, which they had not been able to obtain by their own strength, but which Allah gave them by His power and planning.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 48, verse 21:

﴿Wa-ukhra lam taqdiru ... kulli shay'in qadira﴾ (48:21) "And other spoils which you have not yet been able to win, but which Allah has encompassed. And Allah is over all things capable." Regarding the word "other" (ukhra), the narrations differ: does it refer to the conquest of Makkah? Or the conquest of Khaybar? Or the conquests of the kingdoms of Caesar and Chosroes? Or does it refer to all the conquests that the Muslims attained after the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah?

It is more appropriate that it refers to the conquest of Makkah, because it came after the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah, and it was the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah that provided the causes for this conquest. This treaty could remain in force only for two years. After that, the polytheists of Makkah broke the pact. Thus Allah smoothed the way for this conquest, and Makkah was conquered without battle. It was Makkah that used to launch armies against the Muslims, fighting right inside the homes of the Muslims, and at Hudaybiyyah too it was the one that turned the Muslims back without their having performed ʿUmrah. Allah encompassed it, and without battle it came into their possession.

﴿Wa-kana Allahu ʿala kulli shay'in qadira﴾ (48:21) "And Allah is over all things capable." This too was in fact a veiled glad tidings. At that time Allah had not revealed it, and it was among the unseen matters that had not yet become manifest. Here it is pointed to so that people would be content, hopeful, and happy.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 48, verse 22:

Until this point, Allah had given them glad tidings of the present spoils of war, and also of the spoils that would come after it, and the Muslims began to wait for them. Along with these glad tidings, a great glad tiding was also given: that, God willing, the Muslims would remain victorious and triumphant. The truce that was concluded that year was not arranged because the Muslims were weak, or because the polytheists were very powerful; rather, it was arranged because of certain wisdoms. Had there been a clash with the people of Makkah on that occasion as well, they would have suffered defeat, because the wisdom of Allah requires that when a Muslim and a disbeliever meet at a decisive point, the Muslim should be victorious.

﴿And if those who disbelieved had fought against you, they would surely have turned their backs; then they would have found no protector or helper.﴾ (48:22)

﴿This is the way of Allah which has already taken place before; and you will not find any change in the way of Allah.﴾ (48:23)

Thus Allah links the victory of the believers and the defeat of the disbelievers to the sunnah (way) that operates in this universe, and in which there is no alteration. How great is this tranquillity! How great is this assurance! How great is the steadfastness being granted to these believers, that they were hearing in the Word of Allah, through the words of His Prophet, the glad tidings of their own victory and the defeat of the disbelievers!

Allah's sunnah never changes. Yes, in accordance with His sunnah, the victory may be delayed. This is because the causes of victory are connected with the preparation and training of the believers, and knowledge of their full preparation and proper training rests with Allah alone; or it depends on the arrival of circumstances in which the means and conditions of help and victory for the believers become available and the defeat of the disbelievers becomes certain, so that the importance and impact of the victory may be widened; or there may be other reasons which Allah alone knows. In any case, according to the divine sunnah, victory belongs to the truth, and Allah's sunnah never changes.

"And you will not find any change in the way of Allah." (48:23) Now Allah says that this was the wisdom: in the valley of Makkah, Allah did not grant the disbelievers the ability to lay hands on the Muslims, and He also did not grant the Muslims the ability to lay hands on the Mushrikin of Makkah at a time when they had come under their control. This is a reference to those forty men, forty or more or less, who came to harm the Muslims. They were captured, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) pardoned them.

This was an event that had already taken place, and the listeners knew it well. Allah refers to it in a manner that shows that whatever events occurred, the planning and decree of Allah were at work in them. Through this, the Qur'an was deepening in their hearts the sense that the hand of Allah was arranging matters for them, and that their leadership, through the Messenger of Allah, lay in the hand of Allah. Allah also controls their inclinations so that they become devoted to Allah, surrender their selves to Allah, and have no hesitation regarding the commands of Allah. They should not look this way or that, but should enter fully into Islam. They should hand over their feelings, their emotions, their direction and their activities to Allah, and be certain that all affairs are in the hand of Allah, that goodness is what Allah chooses, and that they are moving in accordance with the power and will of Allah. Whether they accept a matter or reject it, Allah nonetheless desires the welfare of the Muslims. So now, if they bow their heads before the commands of Allah, this welfare will be attained with great ease. Allah is All-Knowing and All-Seeing. He knows what is apparent and what is hidden, and with knowledge and insight He prescribes a path for them. He will never let them be ruined, nor does Allah withhold from them anything that they deserve.

﴿And Allah is Seeing of what you do﴾ (48:24): "And Allah is seeing of what you do."

Sayyid Qutb's commentary on Surah 48, verse 25 (Urdu translation of Fi Zilal al-Quran)

Now Allah comments on the opposing camp of the Muslims: what are their days and nights by Allah's measure? And in what light does Allah view their actions? They are preventing the believers from the Sacred Mosque, and in what light is Allah viewing the Muslims, and in what light (is He viewing) their enemies!

﴿They are the ones who disbelieved and barred you from al-Masjid al-Haram and (prevented) the offering from reaching its place of sacrifice. And were it not for believing men and believing women whom you did not know, whom you might have trampled, and thereby a sin would have affected you without knowledge (you would not have been held back. You were held back so that) Allah may admit into His mercy whom He wills. If they had been separated, We would have punished those who disbelieved among them with a painful punishment. When those who disbelieved had put into their hearts hadiyat al-jahiliyyah (zealotry of ignorance), Allah sent down His tranquility upon His Messenger and upon the believers and caused them to adhere to the word of righteousness, and they were more deserving of it and worthy of it. And Allah is ever Knowing of all things.﴾ (48:25-26)

By Allah's measure, they are undoubtedly disbelievers, and therefore they deserve this detestable title.

﴿They are the ones who disbelieved﴾ (48:25). Allah bestows this title upon them, as though the disbelievers are precisely these people of Makkah. Since this attribute has them immersed in disbelief up to their ears, they are the most detestable creatures before Allah, because Allah regards disbelief as extremely detestable. Then the second evil act they are committing is that they are preventing the believers from the Sacred Mosque, and they are also preventing the sacrificial animals from being taken to their place of slaughter.

﴿And (they) barred you from al-Masjid al-Haram and (prevented) the offering from reaching its place of sacrifice﴾ (48:25). This act is a major sin in Islam, and it was also a sin in the Jahiliyyah. Every religion that passed through the Arabian Peninsula since Ibrahim (peace be upon him) regarded these as major sins. According to their customs, their beliefs, and the religion of the Muslims, these were detestable acts. Therefore, Allah did not restrain the Muslims from attacking them because their crimes were minor; by no means. Rather, there was another wisdom behind it. Out of His kindness, Allah reveals this wisdom.

﴿And were it not for believing men and believing women whom you did not know﴾ (48:25). There were some weak and feeble Muslims remaining in Makkah who had not yet migrated, and who, living among the polytheists, had concealed their Islam out of fear. If war had begun and the Muslims had attacked Makkah, not knowing who was a Muslim and who was a disbeliever, it was possible that these Muslims would have trampled and killed those weak Muslims. Then the disbelievers would have said that the Muslims had not even spared their own people, and thus the Muslims would have had to pay the blood money for the Muslims whom they had killed by mistake. Furthermore, one wisdom was that some of those disbelievers who were now preventing the Muslims from performing Umrah and from taking the sacrificial animals to the place of slaughter were going to become great Muslims among them, and were going to enter into Allah's mercies, and Allah knew all of them. Although these people, had they been separated, Allah would certainly have permitted (the attack), yet Allah had not yet separated them. Therefore, on that occasion Allah saved the disbelievers from that blow.

﴿Allah may admit into His mercy whom He wills. If they had been separated, We would have punished those who disbelieved among them with a painful punishment﴾ (48:25). Thus Allah reveals to this distinct community some aspects of His wisdoms, which lie behind His planning, His decree, and His guidance.

After describing the outward condition of those who disbelieved and their outward deeds, now (follows) the mention of the inner condition of these souls.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 48, verse 26:

﴿When those who disbelieved had put into their hearts hMiyya, the hMiyya of ignorance (al-jahiliyya)﴾ (48:26). "This is why, when those disbelievers placed in their hearts the zealotry of ignorance..." They were not fighting for any ideology or any system; rather, they were ardent upholders of arrogance, pride, rebelliousness and obstinacy. It was because of this zealotry that they opposed the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). They were preventing him from visiting the Sacred Mosque, and they also held back the sacrificial animals that he had brought for this very purpose, so that they might go to the place of sacrifice and be slaughtered there. By this act these people were trampling underfoot every creed and every custom. Merely so that the Arabs would not say that Muhammad (ﷺ) had entered Makkah by force, they were committing such a detestable act, which was itself regarded as detestable among their own people. Then, they themselves were violating the sanctity of the House of Allah, upon which their entire economy depended. Moreover, these people also broke the sanctity of the Sacred Months, which were respected among them and were also respected in Islam. It was this zealotry that made them revile all those who advised them not to prevent Muhammad (ﷺ) from performing 'Umrah. Then, because of this same zealotry of ignorance, Suhayl ibn 'Amr insisted that instead of "Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim" they write "Bismika Allahumma", and then he had the words "Rasul Allah (ﷺ)" struck out and had "Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah" written instead. All these matters were emerging from the very wellspring of that arrogant and proud ignorance.

Allah had placed this ignorant zealotry in their souls because Allah knew that these people were extremely harsh and rebellious. Allah protected the Muslims from this zealotry of ignorance, and in its place sakinah (tranquillity) and the fear of God took its position.

﴿And Allah sent down His tranquillity upon His Messenger and upon the believers, and made them adhere to the word of taqwa (God-consciousness), and they were most deserving of it and worthy of it﴾ (48:26). Sakinah refers to a state of dignity and composure, just as taqwa means a cautious and humble manner. Both of these qualities are found in the believer who is connected to his Lord, who is content with that connection, who trusts in Allah, and who fears Allah in every movement. Therefore he stays away from arrogance and rebelliousness. And when Allah commands him to halt and to cool down, he obeys with complete willingness and tranquillity.

This is why the believers were deserving of being described as people of taqwa, and they were indeed worthy of it. This is a new description of the believers; and the earlier statement that tranquillity was sent down upon them was also an honour for them, because sakinah includes both dignity and taqwa. So it was sent down because they were truly worthy of it by Allah's standards. And Allah Himself bears witness to this. Allah's testimony to the Muslims that they deserve this is another honour, and it has come from Allah.

﴿And Allah is All-Knowing of everything﴾ (48:26).

The earlier passage has already noted that some believers who left Madinah after hearing the Messenger of Allah's (ﷺ) dream were deeply distressed that they could not enter al-Masjid al-Haram that year, and that they were turned back from it. Here the truth of that dream is confirmed: it came from Allah and it was true. It is going to be fulfilled, and something greater than it is yet to come.

As for the good news that they would enter al-Masjid al-Haram in peace, shave their heads and trim their hair, and perform 'umrah without fear, this was fulfilled a year later. It was fulfilled in its fuller form two years after the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah, when Makkah itself was conquered and the religion of Allah and the Islamic order were established throughout Makkah.

However, Allah also teaches the believers Islamic etiquette, and so He says: ﴿Indeed, you will enter al-Masjid al-Haram, if Allah wills, in security﴾ (48:27). Entering al-Masjid al-Haram is certain, since Allah has given the information, but Muslims should make the will of Allah a part of their consciousness and regard it as unrestricted, so that it settles in their hearts that what happens is what Allah wills. The believers should make this a part of their way of thinking. The Qur'an also repeatedly mentions this and makes all decisions subject to the will of Allah. Even where Allah's promises are mentioned, they are conditioned upon the will of Allah. Although Allah never goes against His promises, the will of Allah is free of every restriction. Therefore Muslims should fix this reality in their hearts, so that the foundation of their thinking rests upon ﴿if Allah wills﴾.

Now, how did this promise become reality? The narrations report that in the seventh year of Hijrah, in the month of Dhu al-Qa'dah, that is, after the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) set out for Makkah to perform 'umrah. All the people of Hudaybiyyah were with him. He put on the ihram (the sacred state of consecration for pilgrimage) at Dhu al-Hulayfah and took the hady (sacrificial animals) with him, just as in the previous year he had put on ihram from this same place and taken animals with him. He and his Companions set out reciting the talbiyah (the chant "Labbayk Allahumma labbayk"). When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ,.... drew near, he sent Muhammad ibn Maslamah ahead with horses and weapons. When the polytheists saw them, they were greatly alarmed. They thought that perhaps the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) intended to fight them, and that he had broken the agreement between them, which was that there would be no war for ten years. These men went and warned the people of Makkah. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) arrived and camped at Marr al-Zahran, he sent all the weapons, arrows and spears to Batn Ajij, and from there he proceeded toward Makkah with his swords in their scabbards, as had been agreed with them.

While he was on the way, the Quraysh sent Mikraz ibn Hafs, who came to the Messenger (ﷺ) and said: "We have never heard that you have broken a covenant." He (ﷺ) said: "What do you mean?" He said: "You have come with weapons, spears and arrows, and so on." He (ﷺ) said: "That is not so. We have sent them to Batn Ajij." He said: "That is correct. Our information about you is that you are righteous and God-fearing, and also that you keep your covenants."

The chiefs of the disbelievers left Makkah so that their eyes would not fall upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), for they could not even bear to look at him. As for the ordinary people of Makkah, men, women and children, they sat along the roads and on the rooftops, watching the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his Companions. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) entered Makkah with his Companions walking before him, all of them reciting the talbiyah. All the animals were sent ahead to Dhi Tuwa. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was riding his she-camel al-Qaswa', the same one he had ridden on the day of Hudaybiyyah. 'Abdullah ibn Rawahah, one of the Ansar, held her reins and led her along.

So the dream of the Messenger ﷺ came true. Allah's promise was fulfilled, and the following year the conquest of Makkah took place, and the religion of Allah prevailed over Makkah as well. After that it prevailed throughout the entire Arabian Peninsula (Jazirat al-Arab). Now the final glad tidings were fulfilled in this way:

﴿It is He who has sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth, that He may make it prevail over all religion; and sufficient is Allah as Witness.﴾ (48:28)

Islam did not prevail only in the Arabian Peninsula. It prevailed throughout the world, and this process was completed within the span of half a century. This religion prevailed over the entire realm of Kisra (the Persian emperor), and it conquered a large part of the realm of Qaysar (the Byzantine emperor). It also prevailed in India and China. Then it prevailed in South Asia and Malaya, and it prevailed in Indonesia. This was the world that was inhabited in that era, that is, in the sixth and seventh centuries CE. However, the religion of Allah remains dominant over all other religions to this day, although in those parts of the world where Muslims had political dominance, Muslims have retreated, especially from Europe and the islands of the Mediterranean (Bahr al-Abyad). Muslims have also retreated before the new powers that have arisen in the East and the West.

Yet it is a reality that the religion of truth, that is, Islam, as a religion, still prevails over all religions today. This religion defends itself, through its own essence, its own nature, and its own inherent capacities and excellences, against those who would oppose it, without the sword and without the backing of any political power, and it continues to advance. This is because the nature of this religion is in harmony with the natural laws (nawamis-i-fitrat), and the laws of nature are the true principles that Allah has deposited in this universe. Moreover, this religion has taken into account the needs of the intellect, the soul, and the body alike. The requirements of human development and progress, the needs of society, and the needs of the individual have all been kept in view. The needs of the dweller of a hut and the dweller of a palace or a mansion have all been fulfilled in this religion.

If the followers of other religions were to consider this religion with eyes free from prejudice, they would come to know that it is a religion of great power. It can still provide true guidance to humanity, and in this advanced age it can fulfill the needs of any progressive society with remarkable steadfastness.

﴿And sufficient is Allah as Witness.﴾ (48:28)

In short, less than a century had not passed after the advent of the Prophet when Allah's promise was proven true in political terms, and this religion prevailed over the whole world, and in terms of its own essence it still prevails over all religions. Indeed, all other religions have disappeared from the world, and this is the one religion that endures and remains by virtue of its own inherent capacity, and in terms of its practicality it is always applicable.

Today only the followers of this religion are deprived of the realization of this truth, that Islam prevails by virtue of its own essence. Meanwhile, the enemies of this religion know this and fear it greatly, and they keep the danger of Islam in view in their political policies.

This is the closing part of the surah, and the Qur'an now draws a portrait of the Companions as they actually were at that time. This is the honoured group about whom it was already mentioned earlier that Allah was pleased with them, and the news of Allah's pleasure was conveyed to every single member of this group. Who were these people? Listen!

﴿Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and those who are with him are severe against the disbelievers and merciful among themselves. You see them bowing and prostrating, seeking the bounty of Allah and His pleasure. The marks of prostration are on their faces, by which they are distinguished. This is their description in the Torah, and their example in the Gospel is that of a seed which sends out its shoot, then strengthens it, then it becomes firm, and stands upon its stalk, pleasing the sowers, so that through them Allah may enrage the disbelievers. Allah has promised forgiveness and a great reward to those among them who believe and do righteous deeds﴾ (48:29).

This is a tremendous portrait. The Qur'an draws it in an extraordinarily unique manner. The prominent features of this group are given here: their outward conditions, their hidden spiritual conditions, their mutual relations, and their relations with the disbelievers.

﴿Severe against the disbelievers, merciful among themselves﴾ (48:29). And in the worship and service of Allah:

﴿You see them bowing and prostrating﴾ (48:29). And what their inner state, desire and thought are, what their interests are:

﴿Seeking the bounty of Allah and His pleasure﴾ (48:29). And what their outward features and marks are, how their faces are radiant:

﴿The marks of prostration are on their faces﴾ (48:29). And these same qualities are described in the Torah and the Gospel as well:

(1) ﴿Like a seed which sends out its shoot﴾ (48:29). (2) ﴿Then strengthens it﴾ (48:29). (3) ﴿Then it becomes firm﴾ (48:29). (4) ﴿And stands upon its stalk﴾ (48:29). (5) ﴿It pleases the sowers﴾ (48:29). (6) ﴿So that through them Allah may enrage the disbelievers﴾ (48:29).

Here, first of all, the attribute of Muhammad is affirmed and emphasised, which Suhayl ibn 'Amr had denied, namely that the words "Messenger of Allah" should not be written with the name of the Prophet ﷺ, i.e., "Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah" (ﷺ). After this, the unique and remarkable portrait of the Companions begins, in an extraordinarily unique manner.

The circumstances of believers differ, but the qualities mentioned in these glimpses are found in the lives of all believers, and they are the fundamental points of their lives. From these points the outlines of this portrait emerge, which is extremely beautiful and radiant. Here Allah has given glimpses in which the matters that bring honour to this group are highlighted. Therefore, those points and outlines through which they received honour in the higher realm are prominent here. The first glimpse and hue of their being honoured and esteemed is that these people:

﴿Are severe against the disbelievers and merciful among themselves﴾ (48:29). They are extremely severe against the disbelievers, although at that time their fathers, brothers, close relatives and friends were among the disbelievers. Yet they severed all such ties at once. And they are compassionate among themselves, although between them there is only religious brotherhood. Therefore their severity is also for the sake of Allah, and their gentleness is also for the sake of Allah. This is ideological zeal, Islamic zeal, religious honour. Therefore they desire nothing for their own selves, and there is nothing in this religion for their selves. Thus they are building and shaping their emotions, their loves, their relations and conduct upon the foundation of their beliefs and convictions. They are severe upon their ideological enemies and soft like silk toward their ideological friends. They have become free of egotism and carnal desires. They do not become agitated for anyone or any relation except Allah.

Now the second glimpse: their honour and dignity lie in their bowing and prostration. When they worship, they are in bowing and prostration, and you will always find them in that state, as if this quality is their permanent characteristic. In worship, bowing and prostration are the complete state, and their minds too are in this state, and their bodies too are in bowing and prostration at all times, as if their whole life and whole time is spent in this work.

The third glimpse shown of them is the state of their inner being, their spirituality and their psychology.

﴿You will find them seeking the bounty and pleasure of Allah﴾ (48:29). This is the permanent state of their consciousness. The things their hearts are constantly occupied with, and the longings that rise within them at all times, are only this: that somehow Allah may be pleased. Apart from seeking Allah's pleasure and His bounty, they have no other occupation or interest.

And the fourth quality: their acts of worship are visibly apparent in their features and their outward appearance.

﴿The marks of their prostration are on their faces, by which they are distinguished﴾ (48:29). That is, light, radiance and brilliance will be seen in their faces, and their faces will be clear and pure, because of their pure, living and soul-refreshing worship. The "marks" here do not mean the well-known mark (the mihrab-like spot) that falls on the foreheads of some people (when they rub their foreheads in prostration). The words ﴿from the effect of prostration﴾ may bring that sign to the mind, but "the effect of prostration" means "the effect of worship". Because prostration is the perfection of worship, servitude and obedience, and in it a person is in the perfect state of humility and submission. The effect of this state also becomes apparent on a person's face, because from the faces of worshippers pride, arrogance and intoxication depart, and in their place come noble humility, pure and clear conduct, dignified light and the subdued quality of piety, by which the face of the believer appears extremely beautiful, while despair is entirely absent from it, and he appears happy and content.

This bright portrait that appears in these glimpses is not a new portrait. It is written for them in the system of decree and destiny. It is recorded in the Preserved Tablet. And for this reason its mention has come in the Torah too, and good news about them was given to humankind before they were born upon this earth.

﴿That is their description in the Torah, and their example in the Gospel﴾ (48:29).

In those two earlier books Allah has praised Muhammad ﷺ and his companions thus, that they are:

﴿Like a seed which sends out its shoot﴾ (48:29). They grew in the way a crop sends out its shoots at the beginning; they are fresh and green, and they gradually grow and become strong.

﴿Then strengthens it﴾ (48:29). That is, the shoot strengthened it, or the stalk strengthened it.

﴿Then it becomes firm﴾ (48:29). That is, the stalk and the crop became ever firmer.

﴿And stands upon its stalk﴾ (48:29). That is, the crop stood upon its stalk, its stem or its stalk; now there is neither weakness in it nor bending; it is firm and upright.

This is the condition of the crop itself. But what are its effects on the farmer's soul? What are its effects on the experts who know both the one that grows and the one that withers, both the fruitful and the fruitless? Joy runs through the hearts of such people.

﴿It pleases the sowers﴾ (48:29). In some readings, in place of "al-zurra'" (the farmers) the word "al-zari'" (the sower) appears, and it means the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who is the farmer of this growing, strong, fresh and joy-giving crop. Then what are its effects on the hearts of the disbelievers? Anger and vexation.

﴿So that through them Allah may enrage the disbelievers﴾ (48:29). By mentioning the anger of the disbelievers at the end, the Qur'an has indicated that one should not apply it to the harvest of people. It refers to the harvest of the people of Allah, and the harvest of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and it is the harvest of those who are the instruments of the hand of divine power, and a cause of distress for the disbelievers.

This example too is not a new example; it is recorded in the pages of the Book of Destiny. For this reason its mention is found in the Torah and the Gospel even before Muhammad ﷺ came to the earth and was sent as a messenger. And in the Gospel there is explicit mention that Muhammad and his companions would come.

Thus Allah records the qualities of this group in His everlasting Book, that is, the group of the Companions. Thus this group is established at the centre of this universe. The whole universe moves along with it, and this group hears this praise of its from the Lord. Then the qualities of these people are recorded as a model for coming generations, so that the coming generations too may strive to establish this standard, so that faith may be established at its highest levels.

After this honour and esteem of the Companions' qualities, the announcement is made that there is a great reward for them.

﴿Allah has promised those among them who believe and do righteous deeds forgiveness and a great reward﴾ (48:29). After the qualities of this group, now there is a general announcement, and among those who benefit from this announcement, clearly the first to be included are they. Forgiveness and a great reward. This single announcement is itself a great honour for them, and for them the pleasure of Allah is itself the great reward; but the grace and generosity of Allah are without bounds and without limits, and the forgiveness of Allah is boundless and unlimited.

Once again I open the eye of imagination and look at this honoured group whose hearts are blessed, who are receiving these streams of mercy, honour and promises of a great reward from Allah. It is being recited to them: this announcement that in the books of Allah, in the measures of Allah, and in the halls of Allah, this is for them, this is for them. They are returning from Hudaybiyyah, amid the dust raised by the pace of the camels; they hear this surah, and now it is their spirit and their life. It is descending into their ears and souls. They look at one another and smile, and their very existence is the embodied grace and generosity of Allah... I wish, in the eye of imagination, to look at them and walk a few steps with them. Let me also walk a few steps with them, but how can one who has not walked their path share in this festival of victory? No, he will keep watching from afar... O Allah! You alone can grant someone this honour, that he does not watch salvation from afar but plunges into this celebration. O Allah, You know that I am eager to plunge into this celebration!
